title: Walk It Off with Ronnie
description: Late-night health advice on Snazzie FM. Real listeners send in real ailments. Ronnie reads them aloud and prescribes exactly one cure, no matter what: walk it off. Barry tries to stop him.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're up late, you're not feeling great, you're on Snazzie FM. It's Walk It Off, the only health show that listens. I've got a stack of letters and a heart full of answers.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I want it noted that I am not a doctor, and neither, legally, is Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Noted and overruled, Barry. First letter. Dolores from the bowling alley writes, quote, I rolled my ankle on the lane and now it's swollen, purple, and I can't put any weight on it. Should I see a doctor or just ice it? Unquote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Dolores, sweetheart, that's not an injury. That's confidence. Your body is showing off. <p:0.3> So here's the plan. Get back on the lane, league night if you can swing it, and walk it off.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, that is, that is exactly how ankles get worse.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Worse, better, it's all walking, Barry. Next letter.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: This one's an email. Marcus, an overnight nurse, writes, quote, I haven't slept properly in months on rotating shifts, my hands shake, and I'm scared I'll make a mistake at work. How do I fix my sleep schedule? Unquote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Marcus, great question, and have I got the answer. Reach for an ice-cold Liquid Rage, our sponsor, tonight's official energy of being awake against your will. <p:0.3> See, exhaustion is just walking you haven't done yet. So between rounds, walk it off.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He operates on people, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then he'll be moving anyway. Efficient. Next!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Voicemail transcript, this one. Pat from the dental district. Quote, a tooth's been throbbing for a week, my cheek is swelling, there's a bad taste, and I can't get a dentist for a month. What do I do in the meantime?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You know, Pat, that reminds me of my back. My back's been a saga. Started in ninety-eight, lower lumbar, and let me tell you, the things I've tried. Heat, a magnet, a guy named Sergio.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Pat asked about a tooth.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Right, the tooth. See, an infection, Pat, that's just trapped energy. So here's what you do. Walk it off, briskly, jaw clenched the whole time, to pump it out.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's an abscess, Ronnie, that can spread to the, the actual brain.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then he'll walk it off all the way up there. Moving on.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Letter from Yvonne. Quote, my surgeon told me to rest for six weeks after my operation, but I'm bored and restless. Is it okay to start light activity early? Unquote.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Yvonne, finally, someone who gets it. Six weeks is a suggestion. <p:0.3> Those stitches? Think of them like a seatbelt. And you're allowed to take a seatbelt off. Walk it off, starting tonight. Stairs optional, but encouraged.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: No. No, Yvonne, do not do that. Yvonne, if you can hear me, leave the seatbelt on.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Barry's nervous tonight, folks. He gets like this. <p:0.3> Last letter. And Barry, you read this one, it's a serious one.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Gerald, from the cardiac ward waiting room. Quote. My chest has been tight, my left arm is tingling, and my doctor used the words heart murmur. I'm frightened. Ronnie, what should I do right now? Unquote. <p:0.3> Ronnie. Please get this one right.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Gerald. Deep breath. A murmur, that's just the heart whispering. It's shy. <p:0.3> So here's the full prescription. Walk it off. Then walk it off harder. And if it really persists?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, do not.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Walk it off until it's somebody else's problem. <p:0.3> You're welcome, Gerald.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Oh, before we go. This just came in from Dolores. She says she took your advice last week, walked off the ankle, and now she's writing from the same hospital as Gerald. <p:0.3> They've got her on the murmur ward. She says hi.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, Barry? The walking's working. Tell her to keep it up.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: She's in a bed, Ronnie. Same ward as Gerald. <p:0.3> That's the whole listenership in one room now. Goodnight.
